qt: to the Commission Daniel Buda (PPE), Dan-Ştefan Motreanu (PPE) Subject:

The recent cyber-attacks that hit supermarket refrigeration systems in the Netherlands, Belgium and France have highlighted the vulnerability of food supply chains to hybrid threats and digital infrastructure disruptions. These attacks shut down thousands of refrigerators, spoiled food stocks and highlighted the growing dependence of the agri-food sector on interconnected IT systems. Threats of this kind have serious repercussions for food security, the integrity of supply chains and the resilience of the internal market. 1.

Does the Commission’s EU food security assessment envisage a scenario in which food production, import and distribution chains in the Union are attacked simultaneously? If this is the case, what measures would be implemented to prevent such cyber-attacks from aggravating the current food crisis and fuelling further price hikes?

Does the Commission plan to establish minimum requirements for large food retailers and cold store operators – including as regards back-up systems, manual operating procedures and contingency plans – with a view to ensuring business continuity in case of IT disruptions and minimising food losses?
